rubric.why: Identifies magnitude alone as the defining feature of a scalar.
rubric.description: States that a scalar quantity is described completely by its magnitude only.
rubric.how: Look for both “magnitude” and “only” in the scalar definition.

rubric.why: Identifies both magnitude and direction as necessary for a vector.
rubric.description: States that a vector needs magnitude as well as direction to be described completely.
rubric.how: Look for “magnitude” and “direction” in the vector definition.

modelAnswer: A scalar is a physical quantity that can be described completely by its magnitude only. A vector is a physical quantity that needs magnitude as well as direction to be described completely.

rubric.why: States how the representative lines are arranged for vector addition.
rubric.description: Redraws the vectors so the head of one representative line coincides with the tail of the next.

rubric.why: Gives the direction and endpoints of the resultant vector.
rubric.description: States that the resultant is directed from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last.
rubric.how: Look for the resultant and its direction from the first tail to the last head.

modelAnswer: To add vectors, redraw their representative lines so the head of one coincides with the tail of the next. The resultant is directed from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantities whose relation is shown by a distance-time graph.
rubric.description: States that a distance-time graph shows the relation between distance and time.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantities whose relation is shown by a speed-time graph.
rubric.description: States that a speed-time graph shows the relation between speed and time.

modelAnswer: A distance-time graph shows the relation between distance S and time t. A speed-time graph shows the relation between speed v and time t.

rubric.why: Defines distance using the actual path travelled.
rubric.description: States that distance is the length of the actual path of motion.
rubric.how: Look for “actual path” and its length.

rubric.why: Includes the shortest separation between the endpoints and the direction of displacement.
rubric.description: States that displacement is a vector whose magnitude is the shortest distance between initial and final positions, directed from initial to final.
rubric.how: Look for shortest distance, initial and final positions, and direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the length of the actual path of motion. Displacement is a vector whose magnitude is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions and whose direction is from the initial position to the final position.

rubric.why: Defines speed as distance covered per unit time.
rubric.description: States that the distance covered in unit time is called speed.
rubric.how: Look for distance covered and unit time.

rubric.why: Defines velocity using net displacement per unit time.
rubric.description: States that the net displacement of a body in unit time is called velocity.
rubric.how: Look for net displacement and unit time.

modelAnswer: The distance covered in unit time is known as speed. The net displacement of a body in unit time is called velocity.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantity changing as velocity.
rubric.description: States that acceleration concerns a change in velocity.

rubric.why: Specifies that the velocity change is measured with respect to time.
rubric.description: States that acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity.
rubric.how: Look for the time rate of change of velocity.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is defined as the time rate of change of velocity.
